final.risk: A pandemic-induced credit shock resulting in a self-reinforcing contraction in global mobility, consumer spending, and supply chains [D01].
final.market_implied_probability: Market is currently repricing risk as evidenced by a 3.35% drop in the S&P 500 and a ~46% increase in the VIX to ~25, but does not yet fully reflect a severe systemic credit crisis [D02].
final.our_probability_and_why: We believe there is an underpriced risk of a paradigm-shifting shock; while international clusters are emerging [D01], the market only recently transitioned from complacency [D02], and we view the probability of a severe economic interruption as sufficiently high to warrant protection [D01].
final.instrument: Credit default swaps (CDS) on investment-grade and high-yield indices [D03].
final.exit_rule: Monetize when the risk is clearly priced in or the threat passes, as indicated by a normalization of credit spreads or a change in the infectious disease trajectory [D03, D06].
final.memo:
On February 24, we face a shift from a localized Chinese supply-chain concern to a global pandemic risk with emerging clusters in Italy and South Korea [D01, D07]. Despite the sharp equity market decline, the potential for a self-reinforcing contraction remains a paradigm-shifting threat that is not yet fully discounted by the credit markets [D01, D02].

Our objective is to secure asymmetric liquidity [D04]. By purchasing protection through credit-index CDS, we aim to offset potential portfolio impairments and generate reinvestment capital without liquidating our high-quality, long-term holdings [D03, D04]. We accept a limited, defined premium to protect against a scenario that the market currently misprices as low-probability, maintaining our discipline to exit once the asymmetry is realized or extinguished [D06].
